Bulk archiving cancels each session's active requests before submitting it to its provider. It returns one settled outcome per input session, after every operation has finished, and emits archive lifecycle notifications only for successful outcomes. Providers may implement the optional bulk archive contract to coalesce catalog-change notifications; providers without it receive individual archive calls. A failed session does not prevent independent sessions from being archived, and callers retain successful outcomes for Undo while reporting failures.

+A provider may show a session as archived before its host confirms the archive. It then reports `ISession.archivePending` until the archive settles, ignores earlier host state while it is pending, and restores the session if the host rejects it. Consumers that discard an archived session's state, such as group membership, comparison groups, pins, canvases and terminals, wait for a confirmed archive through `isSessionArchiveConfirmed`.

Worktree cleanup is a shared workbench editor available in both windows. It uses `getSessions({ includeHidden: true })` to include known sessions outside a provider's listing scope, preserving their ownership and shared-checkout protections without broadening the sidebar. Pinning remains profile-local UI state, but cleanup reads persisted pins across profiles, including the Agents profile when that window is closed, and checks them again after confirmation before submitting a batch. Unreadable pin state blocks cleanup rather than treating those sessions as unpinned. In editor windows, the cleanup editor holds the session providers independently of chat or sidebar visibility while it is open or submitting a cleanup batch. Closing it releases the hold only after submission finishes; accepted host cleanup requests continue independently.

Archived inventory discovery is an optional `IChatSessionsService` capability, registered independently of per-environment controllers so it remains reachable before any archived session is known. Management exposes its observable state and disposable demand to Sessions surfaces. Providers without the capability keep their existing discovery behavior; opening a known session does not depend on archive-list demand.

Chats may expose server-published live canvases through an observable provider-neutral collection when the owning provider permits canvas presentation for that session. Each chat discovers membership from its advertised canvas channel references; each subscribed channel supplies presentation metadata and an optional live HTTP(S) source. Unknown membership is distinct from an authoritative empty collection, and pending canvas state retains its resource without a source. Registered canvas-definition listings use the same distinction: `undefined` means the provider registry is unsettled and consumers retain the last authoritative listing, while an empty array authoritatively clears it. A provider that returns `undefined` must publish another canvas change after the registry settles so consumers request the authoritative snapshot. Agent Host providers enable presentation only for durable Copilot sessions; ephemeral sessions expose no canvas capability. Remote sessions expose it only while browser remote proxying is enabled, unless their host is known not to proxy browser connections, so a temporary disconnect keeps their canvases. Canvas execution and presentation continue to follow the existing canvas enablement setting. Session and chat switches suspend presentation while retaining the live browser model, so returning reattaches the same page and browser-side state. Closing presentation dismisses that canvas lifetime without invoking provider operations; archive, deletion, authoritative membership removal, or source replacement releases its browser model. Closing the canvas itself is a separate user operation that names the canvas by its channel. The Agents Window routes it through `ISessionsManagementService` to the owning provider, and the Editor Window through the chat's canvas context; either way the host ends that live canvas and notifies its canvas provider, and the resulting authoritative membership removal releases the presentation. Metadata and source updates do not reopen a dismissed canvas; a later successful model request to open that instance explicitly permits revealing the existing lifetime again. Open-request identity is derived from the owning chat's tool state and is client-only presentation metadata, not a canvas-channel revision. Canvas membership, sources, and browser models are not persisted across restarts. The workbench owns the shared canvas editor, presentation lifecycle, and retained browser models; the Agents Window supplies its active-session/active-chat context, editor working sets, and layout policy, while the Editor Window permits exact owners represented by visible chat widgets.

-A user can pin a live canvas to the Agents Window sidebar. `IPinnedCanvasService` (`contrib/canvases`) keeps each pin live through the optional provider hook `observeCanvas`, routed through `ISessionsManagementService`, which observes one canvas channel without the active-session gate; holding that reference may keep the owning session resident, so pins are capped. The canvas stays owned by its chat, whose agent keeps driving it. Pins persist only identity (provider, session, chat, extension, canvas type, instance ID, and last title) in workspace storage and rebind by instance ID. Activating a pin always shows its canvas page and never the owning chat; a pin that is not connected reconnects through the optional provider hook `observeChatCanvases`, which observes the chat's canvas membership without the active-session gate until the pin binds. A chat can lose a canvas it had open, for example when a lazily activated canvas provider stays dormant after an Agent Host restart, so when a shown pin's chat lacks its canvas, the pin asks the chat to open that instance again through `ISessionsManagementService.openCanvas` and binds once the chat publishes it; if the chat cannot open it or does not publish it in time, the pin shows as unavailable until it is shown again. A request made through a session that goes away or is replaced is abandoned and made again once the session returns. A pin is removed when its session is removed or archived, its chat is deleted, or `ISessionsManagementService.onDidCloseCanvas` reports its canvas closed; closing its tab keeps it. A pinned canvas is shown full-page on the canvas custom view and never opens as an editor in another chat's working set: `ICanvasService.isOwnerPresentable` still governs editors, while `isPresentable` also admits a canvas that the canvas page shows. One canvas view at a time attaches a browser model; a hidden view never takes it from a visible one.

A session can also start with a canvas instead of a request. `ISessionsManagementService.createCanvasDraft` returns an unlisted quick chat from the first provider that implements the optional `ISessionsProvider.createCanvasDraft`; it never replaces the composer's draft. The draft lists the canvases it can open without being started: the host launches the draft's runtime early, as it pre-warms a chat, and lists from it without persisting or announcing anything. Opening a canvas in the draft starts it on the host as its first send would, claiming that runtime, and the provider graduates the draft exactly as a first send does, titled after the canvas. Disposing the draft before a canvas opens, or a canvas that does not open, deletes it. A draft with a workspace cannot do either; its first send creates its worktree. The reference `open` resolves to keeps the new chat's canvases observed until the caller releases it, so the caller can pin the canvas before the session is ever shown.
